newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends lower on late sell-off.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends lower on late sell-off.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - Late selling pulled down prices at the close after a quiet morning session. Activity picked up in the afternoon as players sold off due to technical factors after Jan Fut broke support 1,130 rgt. Next support is at 1,100 rgt.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Selective trading with players still waiting more clearer fundamentals factors.
January futures ended 19 ringgit down at 1,121 ringgit ($447.24) a tonne after opening at 1,145 ringgit. Prices are expected to fall further if there are no fresh demand news.
"January futures is likely to drop to 1,100 ringgit next week if there is lack of big participation and no supportive news," another trader said.
Prices turned easier in the afternoon session mainly on technical selling, after rising initially due to a higher soyoil market in Chicago on talk of buying interest from China.
"The main reason for the quietness in the morning was lack of news," a trader said, adding that no demand was seen."Exports are expected to be slow after a sharp surge in August."
Physicals saw selective dealings in October (south) crude palm oil which was offered at 1,165 ringgit a tonne after trading from 1,160 to 1,165. Oct (south) was bid at 1,160.

Oct (central) was offered at 1,140 and bids at 1,135 and Oct (north) at 1,135 against 1,125. Nov (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,170 ringgit with bids at 1,165. Nov (central) saw offers at 1,150 and bids at 1,137.50 and Dec (south) at 1,175 with bids at 1,165.
In refined palm oil market, Nov/Dec RBD palm oil was offered at $487.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia, and Jan/Feb/Mch at $495.
Nov RBD palm olein saw offers at $520, Dec at $517.50 and Jan/Feb/Mch at $520. Nov was traded from $517.50 to $520, and Jan/Feb/Mch at $517.50.
Oct/Nov RBD palm stearin was offered at $370 and Dec at $375 and Nov/Dec palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $320. - Tan Lee Lee (603-230-7510) ($1=2.5065 ringgit).
